questions.question: What are the four main forces acting on an airplane in flight?
questions.idealAnswer: Lift, weight, thrust, and drag

questions.question: What is directional stability?
questions.idealAnswer: The ability of an aircraft to avoid yawing.

questions.question: What is the term that describes the angle between relative wind and chord line of a wing?
questions.idealAnswer: AOA (Angle of Attack)

questions.question: What are the factors that cause an airplane wing to stall?
questions.idealAnswer: When critical AOA (around 18°) is exceeded causing airflow separation and loss of lift

concepts.label: When critical AOA is exceeded causing airflow separation
terms: when critical aoa is exceeded causing airflow separation

questions.question: What are the principal effects of lowering flaps while in flight?
questions.idealAnswer: Lift and drag increase, stall speed decreases. It allows a steeper descent angle without an increase in airspeed.

concepts.label: stall speed decreases. It allows a steeper descent angle without an increase in airspeed
terms: stall speed decreases. it allows a steeper descent angle without an increase in airspeed

questions.question: What is the function of a wing mounted vortex generator?
questions.idealAnswer: To delay boundary flow separation allowing a higher AOA and delaying the stall (allows for lower stall speeds)

concepts.label: To delay boundary flow separation allowing a higher AOA
terms: to delay boundary flow separation allowing a higher aoa

questions.question: How does blade-flapping help to compensate for dissymmetry of lift in helicopter main rotor systems?
questions.idealAnswer: It increases AOA/lift on the retreating blade and decreases AOA on the advancing blade. (Dissymmetry of lift is unequal thrust created during forward flight by the advancing blade’s higher AOA which creates more lift respective to relative wind than the lower AOA of the retreating blade)

concepts.label: It increases AOA/lift on the retreating blade
terms: it increases aoa/lift on the retreating blade

concepts.label: decreases AOA on the advancing blade
terms: decreases aoa on the advancing blade

questions.question: How does the airflow through the main rotor of a helicopter change during the transition from normal flight to autorotation?
questions.idealAnswer: In normal flight air moves downward from the blades and during autorotation it moves upward through the blades.

concepts.label: In normal flight air moves downward from the blades
terms: in normal flight air moves downward from the blades

concepts.label: during autorotation it moves upward through the blades
terms: during autorotation it moves upward through the blades

questions.question: What is autorotation?
questions.idealAnswer: Autorotation is when the helicopter rotor blades spin without engine power as air flows through the rotor.

questions.question: What is the imaginary line that runs from the leading edge to the trailing edge of an airfoil?
questions.idealAnswer: Chord Line

questions.question: What is the purpose of stall strips on the leading edge of an airplane wing?
questions.idealAnswer: Stall strips cause a disruption to the airflow as an angle of attack increases, causing the inboard section of the wing to stall before the outboard wing

concepts.label: Stall strips cause a disruption to the airflow as an angle of attack increases
terms: stall strips cause a disruption to the airflow as an angle of attack increases

concepts.label: causing the inboard section of the wing to stall before the outboard wing
terms: causing the inboard section of the wing to stall before the outboard wing

questions.question: What is the longitudinal airspeed described as?
questions.idealAnswer: Velocity

questions.question: What is meant by relative wind with regard to an airfoil?
questions.idealAnswer: The direction the wind strikes an airfoil

questions.question: What is meant by the critical angle of attack?
questions.idealAnswer: The highest angle of attack at which the air passes over the airfoil in a smooth flow. Above the critical angle of attack the airflow breaks away and becomes turbulent

concepts.label: The highest angle of attack at which the air passes over the airfoil in a smooth flow. Abo
terms: the highest angle of attack at which the air passes over the airfoil in a smooth flow. above the critical angle of attack the airflow breaks away

questions.question: What is meant by the stagnation point of an airfoil?
questions.idealAnswer: The point on the leading edge of an airfoil at which the airflow separates, some flowing over the top and some over the bottom

concepts.label: The point on the leading edge of an airfoil at which the airflow separates
terms: the point on the leading edge of an airfoil at which the airflow separates

questions.question: What is meant by weight?
questions.idealAnswer: The measure of the force of gravity acting on a body

questions.question: What is meant by thrust?
questions.idealAnswer: The forward aerodynamic force produced by a propeller, fan, or turbojet engine as it forces a mass of air to the rear, behind the airplane

concepts.label: The forward aerodynamic force produced by a propeller
terms: the forward aerodynamic force produced by a propeller

concepts.label: or turbojet engine as it forces a mass of air to the rear
terms: or turbojet engine as it forces a mass of air to the rear

questions.question: What is meant by drag?
questions.idealAnswer: The aerodynamic force acting in the same plane as the relative wind striking an airfoil. Drag acts in the direction opposite to that of thrust

questions.question: What is meant by dissymmetry of lift produced by a helicopter rotor?
questions.idealAnswer: The difference in lift between the two sides of the rotor disc when the helicopter is in forward flight. The side with the advancing blade produces the greater lift because the forward speed adds to the rotor speed. The side with the retreating blade produces less left because the forward speed subtracts from the rotor speed

questions.question: What is meant by a blade stall of a helicopter rotor?
questions.idealAnswer: A condition of flight in which the retreating blade is operating at an angle of attack higher than will allow for the air to flow over its upper surface without turbulence

questions.question: What is meant by translational lift in a helicopter?
questions.idealAnswer: The additional lift produced by a helicopter rotor as the helicopter changes from hovering to forward flight

questions.question: What is meant by ground effect in helicopter flight?
questions.idealAnswer: An increase in lift when a helicopter is flying at an altitude of less than half the rotor span. This increase is produced by the effective increase in the angle of attack caused by the deflection of the downwashed air.

questions.question: What is meant by ground resonance in a helicopter?
questions.idealAnswer: The destructive vibration that occurs when the helicopter touches down roughly and unevenly. The shock throws a load into the lead-lag hinges of the rotor blades and causes them to oscillate about this hinge. If the frequency of this oscillation is the same as the resonant frequency of the fuselage, the energy will cause the helicopter to strike the ground hard with the opposite skid or wheel. If corrective action is not taken immediately, ground resonance can destroy the helicopter

terms: the destructive vibration that occurs when the helicopter touches down roughly

questions.question: How do flaps allow an airplane to take off and land at a slow airspeed?
questions.idealAnswer: The extension of flaps increases the camber of the airfoil, causing greater lift and drag

concepts.label: The extension of flaps increases the camber of the airfoil
terms: the extension of flaps increases the camber of the airfoil

questions.question: Why do slots and slats delay the onset of a stall to a higher angle of attack?
questions.idealAnswer: They allow the airflow to remain attached to the upper surface of the wing at higher angles of attack, reducing stall speed

concepts.label: They allow the airflow to remain attached to the upper surface of the wing at higher angle
terms: they allow the airflow to remain attached to the upper surface of the wing at higher angles of attack

questions.question: What is the function of wing fences on the aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: Wing fences, or stall fences, delay the stall from reaching the ailerons, allowing improved aileron control at slower airspeeds

concepts.label: delay the stall from reaching the ailerons
terms: delay the stall from reaching the ailerons

concepts.label: allowing improved aileron control at slower airspeeds
terms: allowing improved aileron control at slower airspeeds

questions.question: Define matter.
questions.idealAnswer: Any substance that occupies space and has mass.

questions.question: Matter may exist in what three states?
questions.idealAnswer: Solid, liquid and gas.

questions.question: Define kinetic energy.
questions.idealAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.

questions.question: Work is the product of what two factors?
questions.idealAnswer: Force and the distance moved.

questions.idealAnswer: All three states are affected, with gases being affected the most.

questions.question: What is a British Thermal Unit?
questions.idealAnswer: The amount of heat energy required to change the temperature of 1 pound of water 1 degree Fahrenheit.

questions.question: Name the three methods of heat transfer?
questions.idealAnswer: Conduction, convection and radiation.

questions.question: What term defines the temperature at which all molecular motion ceases?
questions.idealAnswer: Absolute zero.

questions.question: Can liquids be compressed?
questions.idealAnswer: No, liquids are generally considered incompressible.

questions.question: What are the customary units used to express hydraulic or pneumatic pressure in the United States?
questions.idealAnswer: Pounds per square inch.

questions.question: Describe how pressure is transmitted when a force is applied to a confined liquid.
questions.idealAnswer: Pressure is transmitted equally in all directions,

questions.question: What formula expresses the relationship between force, pressure and area?
questions.idealAnswer: Force equals area times pressure.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of sound at sea level on a standard day?
questions.idealAnswer: 661 Knots or 340 meters per second.

questions.question: What is the atmospheric pressure at sea level on a standard day?

What are the factors that determine density altitude?

questions.question: What are the four principle forces acting on an airplane in flight?
questions.idealAnswer: Lift, drag, thrust and gravity.

questions.question: What is friction?

questions.question: What are two types of fluids?

questions.question: What is the name of the atmospheric phenomenon where cool air is trapped near the earth by warm air?

questions.question: What is meant by the density of air?
questions.idealAnswer: The mass of a given volume of air.

questions.question: What does specific gravity mean?

questions.question: Name the forms of energy that can be converted into heat energy?
questions.idealAnswer: Mechanical, electrical, chemical, radiant, nuclear, and solar.

questions.idealAnswer: Rolling, Sliding, and Static

questions.question: What is magnetism?
questions.idealAnswer: Motion of an electric charge, resulting in attractive and repulsive forces between objects.
